candidates.title: Driving through the Manila slum
candidates.description: There was a 'clearing' in the traffic so to speak, due to a large water tank blocking half the road, so I dared this more direct shot. You can see people making their living whatever way they can- selling reconditioned computers recovered from scrap, repairing refrigerators etc. It is EXACTLY like this in large cities in India. I was actually feeling a lump in my throat here, and looking at these simple, hard working folk struggling to make ends meet wondered whether the slums of Manila are really such dangerous places after all. After dark maybe, if you flash your valuables. (Manila, Philippines, May 2013)
candidates.creator: shankar s.

candidates.title: Manila, Utah
candidates.description:
Manila is a small town located on the northern edge of Daggett County, Utah, just south of the Wyoming border in the United States. The town is at the junction of State Route 43 and State Route 44, and is the county seat of Daggett County. Nearby sites include the Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area and the Flaming Gorge Reservoir just east of town, and to the south is Ashley National Forest, which includes Kings Peak (13,528 ft), the highest point in Utah.

The population of Manila was 310 at the 2010 census. The settlement was named in 1898, commemorating the American naval victory at the Battle of Manila Bay in the Philippines.

Manila is located in northeastern Utah, north of the Uinta Mountains and west of the Flaming Gorge Reservoir on the Green River. The northern border of the town is the Wyoming state line.

candidates.title: File:Iglesia de San Miguel, Manila, Filipinas, 2023-08-27, DD 29-31 HDR.jpg
candidates.creator: Diego Delso
candidates.description: San Miguel Church‎, formally The Royal Parish and National Shrine of Saint Michael and the Archangels, Manila, Philippines. The shrine is located within the Malacañang Palace complex, the official residence of the President of the Republic of the Philippines. Presidents that have heard Mass at the shrine include Carlos P. García, Gloria Macapagal Arroyo, and Fidel V. Ramos (who was Protestant). The Church was first built in stone in 1603 by the Jesuits in Paco. In 1611, the Jesuits and Filipino Catholics accommodated the Japanese Christians who were persecuted by the Tokugawa Shogunate. It was Blessed Dom Justo Takayama (高山右近), a daimyō or feudal lord, who led a group of approximately 300 Japanese Christians to the Philippines in 1614. The church was damaged in the 1645 Luzon earthquake, and during the British occupation of Manila that was part of the Seven Years' War. The church was rebuilt in 1913. The church served as the pro-cathedral of the Archdiocese of Manila while Manila Cathedral was being rebuilt from 1946 to 1958 following the city's destruction in World War II. It was elevated to the rank of a national shrine in 1986.

candidates.title: File:Compania Maritima Building ruins on the Cebu waterfront.jpg
candidates.creator: Idolwanderer
candidates.description:
Compania Maritima Building ruins on the Cebu waterfront, just south of the Cebu Customs Building, and north of the China Heritage Museum, one block east of Cebu City Hall.  
The building was originally constructed in 1910, the same year as the Cebu Customs Building, making both buildings 114 years old.  The Compania Maritimas Building once housed the Shamrock Hotel & the Manila Steamship Co.  
At some point the top floor lost its entire roof, all the glass window panes are now gone, and the ground floor is sealed shut.  The structure's bright yellow exterior is an empty shell  inside.  On city maps it is referred to as "ruins."  
Oddly, there is no historical marker or plaque at the site. 

Sadly, this site seems tied up in an ownership dispute between the Cebu Port Authority (CPA) and the Cebu City Government that is somehow related to redevelopment plans for the whole Carbon Market area.
